findings: Both captures say a merchant receiving the transaction funds on PayPal uses PayPal account or sFTP reporting to match Stripe payments to PayPal orders. Stripe reconciles the Stripe-settling PayPal transactions before payout. No account-specific settlement or bank arrival follows from the guide. Related November settlement guidance documents direct businesses choosing and Connect settling with Stripe (old 8-13; new 9-14; related preference guide 13-21,39-45).

The preferred merchant reference is an order or invoice ID set at PaymentIntent creation under payment_method_options.paypal.reference. Customers can see it; processed payments show the reference as Invoice ID in the PayPal settlement report and derived refunds or disputes are associated with it. The November example sends a PaymentIntent create request with amount=1099 and currency=eur with automatic methods enabled and this exact option, while May's Node example explicitly selects PayPal (old 17-38; new 18-31).

If a business-generated order ID is unavailable, the fallback uses Charge.payment_method_details.paypal.transaction_id. It is present only after capture and maps the PayPal capture ID to Transaction ID in the settlement report; the example also has captured true and paid true. It is not a payer ID, Stripe Charge ID, or proof that a bank payout arrived (old 40-103; new 33-96).

PayPal business account Activity → All Reports → Transactions → Settlement, or PayPal-enabled sFTP, gives the report covering balance-impacting transactions over 24 hours to reconcile movements in PayPal against the linked bank account (old 105-117; new 98-110).

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-paypal-payout-reconciliation-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-paypal-reconciliation-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-paypal-reconciliation.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paypal/payout-reconciliation`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paypal/payout-reconciliation, a merchant who settles PayPal payments to PayPal manually matches processed payments against its PayPal business report or sFTP feed. Stripe handles transaction reconciliation before payout for the Stripe-settlement route. The merchant sets a customer-visible reference at PaymentIntent creation; it appears as Invoice ID after processing and relates subsequent refunds and disputes. When no business order ID is available, the guide recommends the PayPal transaction_id on a captured Charge, which matches Transaction ID (old raw lines 8-54; new raw lines 9-47). The PayPal report covers 24 hours of balance-impacting transactions. source-stripe-paypal-reconciliation.md has the stable keys but should include each example's selection configuration and scope the fallback as a recommendation. A created Intent or captured Charge does not establish payout arrival.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paypal/payout-reconciliation, the May 7 Node PaymentIntent create example selects PayPal explicitly, whereas the November 7 cURL example enables automatic payment methods. Both send the same PayPal reference, so preserve the settings as dated examples in source-stripe-paypal-reconciliation.md without inferring an API requirement or universal PayPal availability (old raw lines 17-38; new raw lines 18-31). Code language, JSON indentation, buyer/customer terminology and report-list numbering are presentation. Retain the capture condition, Invoice ID versus Transaction ID, related refunds/disputes, and PayPal business account or sFTP access (old raw lines 40-117; new raw lines 33-110). Preserve reciprocal wallet and settlement-preference routes and the distinct Stripe payout report route with its own automatic payout qualifications.
